newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX refined prods drag oil complex to lower end.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX refined prods drag oil complex to lower end.

text.p: Losses in NYMEX refined products quashed a late session rebound in crude and dragged the oil complex to a weaker close Monday, traders said.
"Basically there was some pressure in the last few minutes as length accumulated by the locals gave way to profit-taking and downward pressure by the products," said a dealer in New York.
February crude ended off 29 cents a barrel at $24.79 after clawing back into positive territory minutes before the market's close to make a session high of $25.17.
January heating oil finished off 1.89 cents a gallon at 71.08 cents, and January gasoline ended off 1.29 cents a gallon at 68.90 cents.
Heating oil suffered the worst losses due to warmer-than-expected temperature forecasts while supplies were deemed adequate, traders said.

Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said above average temperatures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States should drop to below normal by late week. But, forecasters had expected a colder average for the week as a whole for that region.
Traders noted volume was particularly thin ahead of the Christmas holiday on Wednesday.
"Volume is dead. You can't really read too much into what's happening today," said a New York trader.
NYMEX will close at 1300 EST Christmas Eve on Tuesday and will reopen for regular trading hours Thursday.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) will release its weekly oil inventory data on Thursday instead of its regulary scheduled time of Tuesday evening since the API will be closed Christmas Eve.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
